title: Crouch End & Hornsey
intro: A Victorian village in a valley below Alexandra Palace and Highgate, with an old railway turned into a woodland walk and a 1930s town hall.

items.name: Crouch End Clock Tower
items.blurb: The red-brick clock tower of 1895 at the heart of the Broadway, surrounded by Victorian and Edwardian shopping parades.
items.tip: Saturday mornings are the liveliest time on the Broadway.

items.name: Priory Park
items.blurb: A neat park on Middle Lane with formal gardens, a fountain, a paddling pool, tennis courts and a café.
items.tip: Good for small children on a summer afternoon.

items.name: Parkland Walk
items.blurb: A disused railway line turned into London's longest local nature reserve, running through cuttings and over bridges towards Highgate and Finsbury Park.
items.tip: Look for the spriggan sculpture in an old arch near the Crouch End end.

items.name: Hornsey Town Hall
items.blurb: A modernist town hall of the 1930s, Grade II* listed, with a square in front that hosts markets and events.
items.tip: Look out for the farmers' and craft markets on the square.
